angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 940,586 km at 147.20 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7933 +/- 0.0109 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 147.20 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.352 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Van Eylen et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-410 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...782...14V/abstract): 940,586 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.214 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Van Eylen et al. 2014, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-410 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...782...14V/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6273 +/- 140 K from Van Eylen et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-410 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...782...14V/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Van Eylen et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-410 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...782...14V/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-410-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.260, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
